problem: Fabs spend billions on cleanrooms and ultra-high-purity nitrogen purges, yet airborne molecular contaminants still reach wafers as features shrink.
business_model: Hardware units installed inside process tools (Talos), with a planned fab interconnect (Cleanpipe); pilot program

founders.name: Noah Vogel
education: University of Michigan, BSE Aerospace Engineering

founders.name: Colin Lavery
education: University of Michigan, BSE Space Sciences and Engineering

competitors.name: Entegris
competitors.what: AMC filters at ambient air inlet and point of use for semiconductor fabs

competitors.name: AAF International
competitors.what: AstroSorb carbon AMC filters for point of use protection of lithography and metrology

competitors.name: Getek
competitors.what: CHEMSORB-R chemical filter series for AMC and VOC removal

technical_complexity.rationale: Destroying contaminants inside tools at 10 to 100 times cleaner levels and qualifying with fab equipment is hard hardware and chemistry work for a four person team.

defensibility.rationale: Once integrated into a tool and qualified, replacement is slow; filter incumbents compete on a different approach (adsorption) rather than reactive destruction.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Filter vendors serve the need today; no response to Aerogen documented.

market_need_then: Entegris and AAF describe AMC as an invisible threat to yield; fabs spend heavily on cleanrooms and nitrogen purge, per the company.

branding.domain_note: Uses aerogensystems.com, not the shorter aerogen.com which belongs to an unrelated medical nebuliser company.

identity.voice_and_tone: Bold vision language: delete the cleanroom

branding.brand_signature: Talos cleans the tools, Cleanpipe connects them
branding.community_and_virality: Won top prize at U-M Impact Venture Demo Day in April 2026 (per a U-M Center for Entrepreneurship post).

brand_strength.rationale: Clear product naming and tagline, but name collides with the Irish medical company Aerogen and there is little press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Aerogen Systems is a Summer 2026 YC spinout of University of Michigan aerospace research that won the university's Demo Day top prize and a Fuel grant. It is piloting Talos in semiconductor tooling and has no disclosed venture funding. The outcome depends on equipment partner pilots and proving lab claims in fabs; unknown for now.
notes: A third party summary says over 500K USD NASA R&D funding; unverified, not recorded as a round. Dealroom 125K and CB Insights 81M USD figures belong to unrelated companies named Aerogen and are ignored. Purity claims conflict across articles (7N vs 8N). Founding year conflicts (2025 vs 2026), left null. Competitor entries are established AMC filter vendors, from 2025 sources.
